title: cross-distro OCI indexing and registry shard support for air-gapped installs
author: Diego Marquez
description:
Motivation: Customers deploying Redwood Private in regulated or disconnected datacenters run into two recurring problems: 1) curated OCI indexes produced by different distro toolchains (k3s, rke2, kubeadm derivatives) use slightly different manifest list layouts and annotations; 2) very large air-gapped sites need a sharded registry seeding approach so that prefetch/seed time, network usage, and disk pressure can be distributed across multiple local registry endpoints and promoted atomically.

This PR implements a cross-distro OCI indexing layer and operator-friendly registry-shard seeding mechanism: it generates a normalized OCI index tuned for each supported distro variant (k3s, rke2, kubeadm, microk8s), supports per-shard GZIP delta manifests for faster syncs, and wires an atomic promotion plan into the installer preflight and upgrade hooks. It also hardens signature verification of the index (cosign) and adds Helm chart values to surface shard topology and signing keys.

Summary of changes (high level):
- Add go/pkg/ociindex: index normalizer that accepts vendor manifests and emits a canonical OCI index + per-distro compatibility shim. Normalizer preserves original digests and emits an index metadata file consumed by the seeder.
- Implement registry sharding in scripts/registry-seed: new --shards N mode that computes shard assignment by image namespace and writes per-shard tarstreams. Includes a --promote-atomic flag that emits a promotion manifest and a small orchestrator script.
- Helm chart changes: charts/redwood-installer/templates/registry-config.yaml and values.yaml additions to declare shards, preseed URLs, and cosign public keys. Chart templates render shard ConfigMaps and initJobs for seeding in on-prem clusters.
- Terraform module: modules/registry-shard creates local registry instances (harbor/registry mirrored sets) + cloud-init snippets for pre-populating signed indexes. The module exposes outputs to wire into the installer CLI for bootstrap.
- Preflight and upgrade hooks: preflight now verifies index signatures, validates shard coverage against requested component set, and simulates promotion if --dry-run. Upgrade hooks perform a two-phase promote with rollback markers for safe rollback.
- Tests: integration test harness in test/integration/registry_shard_test.go (local simulation) and CI job .github/workflows/registry-shard.yaml that runs a fast smoke and cosign verification.

Breaking notes and rationale: the normalizer changes index shape but does not rewrite image digests. The two-phase promotion requires registries to support manifest PUT semantics used by the seeder; the Terraform module emits an optional proxy plugin for registries that need a compatibility layer.

Checklist: 
- [x] Index normalizer implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Seeder supports --shards and --promote-atomic
- [x] Helm chart values and templates updated with defaults for k3s/rke2
- [x] Terraform module for registry shards with examples
- [x] Integration test and CI job added
- [x] Docs: additions to docs/private/airgap-sharding.md and runbook notes for operations (see release_notes)

Testing and verification: ran the integration harness locally: 3-shard simulation with 1.2k images completed in 19m (compared to ~52m single-registry seeding). CI workflow passed (unit + smoke + cosign verification). Manual canary on internal staging (staging-ontap) performed a dry-run promote and then full promote; rollback paths were exercised and produced expected markers.

Upgrade and rollback guidance: the installer will, during upgrades, stage new indexes to per-shard temp prefixes then perform the atomic promote. If any shard fails, the promote script marks a rollback token and the installer runs the reverse promotion using the previously recorded manifest state. The Terraform module includes an example for 'blue/green' shard assignment to limit blast radius.

Backward compatibility: existing non-sharded installs are unaffected unless you opt-in by specifying shard topology in the Helm values or using the --shards flag with the seeder.

Related tickets and follow-ups: ENG-10135 (orchestrator operator to automate promotion scheduling), ENG-10140 (monitoring + metrics for shard health), and a follow-up to add multi-arch crosswalk heuristics for arm64/ppc64.

Files changed summary and illustrative snippet: see changed_files for a high-level listing. Example snippet from go/pkg/ociindex/normalizer.go (abbreviated):

Merge notes: squash-merged to main after approvals and green CI.

Operational docs added: docs/private/airgap-sharding.md contains step-by-step seeding, promote/rollback examples, Terraform usage, and troubleshooting steps.

review_comments: Aisha Patel: Please add a note about how this interacts with existing delta-snapshots; we should avoid double-compression overhead.
Author reply (Diego): Added a note and changed the seeder to prefer existing gzipped blobs when present; updated tests.
Marcus Liu: I ran the integration harness, found a timeout on promote.sh with slower registries. Can we add exponential backoff?
Author reply (Diego): Added backoff and jitter to promote.sh and unit tests for retry behavior.
Evelyn Ross: Security review: cosign public key distribution needs rotation guidance. Add in docs and Helm values for key rotation window.
Author reply (Diego): Doc section for rotation added and Helm values include rotate_window_days with default 90.
release_notes: Added a cross-distro OCI index normalizer and a registry-shard seeder with atomic promotion for faster air-gapped installs. New Terraform module to create local registry shards and Helm chart values to configure shard topology and cosign keys. Includes rollback-safe promotion and integration tests. See docs/private/airgap-sharding.md for migration and operational guidance.
